question: What is the primary natural pacemaker of a healthy human heart?
explanation: The sinoatrial node fires impulses faster than any other part of the conduction system, making it the primary pacemaker that sets the normal heart rate. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T3#GNS213_U1_T3_h1)

question: Why does the electrical signal pause briefly at the AV node during a heartbeat?

options.A: To equalize blood pressure between the left and right sides
options.B: To give the SA node time to recharge its chemical supply
options.C: To prevent the heart muscle from entering complete tetanus
options.D: To allow the atria time to empty blood into the ventricles

explanation: Great job thinking about heart mechanics! That brief pause at the AV node is super important—it makes sure the top chambers (atria) finish squeezing all their blood down before the bottom chambers contract. You've got this! [learn more](GNS213_U1_T3#GNS213_U1_T3_h1)

question: Which electrolyte imbalance is most known for triggering dangerous heart rhythm changes?
explanation: Potassium is a big deal for the heart! It directly helps maintain the electrical charge of heart cells. When potassium levels go out of whack, the heart's electrical system easily gets confused. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T3#GNS213_U1_T3_h2)

question: A patient with coronary artery disease develops a sudden irregular heartbeat. What is the link between the disease and this rhythm change?

options.A: Coronary blockages directly destroy the sinoatrial node cells
options.B: Ischemia damages the heart's electrical conduction pathways
options.C: Narrowed arteries cause the heart to beat faster to compensate
options.D: Fatty plaques physically block electrical signals from traveling

explanation: When coronary arteries are narrowed, the heart muscle gets less oxygen (ischemia). Stressed, oxygen-starved heart cells have a hard time passing electrical signals smoothly, leading to irregular rhythms. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T3#GNS213_U1_T3_h2)

question: Which heart rhythm is a life-threatening emergency that requires immediate CPR and defibrillation?
explanation: Ventricular fibrillation (V-fib) is a true medical emergency! The lower chambers just quiver instead of pumping, meaning no blood flows. Quick CPR and a shock are literal lifesavers here. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T3#GNS213_U1_T3_h3)

question: What is the main difference between atrial fibrillation and a normal sinus rhythm?

options.A: The electrical signal travels backward from the purkinje fibers
options.B: The upper chambers quiver chaotically instead of contracting effectively
options.C: The heart rate drops permanently below forty beats per minute
options.D: The lower chambers stop receiving blood from the lungs entirely

explanation: In atrial fibrillation (A-fib), the upper chambers (atria) don't squeeze neatly—they kind of jitter or quiver instead. Think of it as a shaky handshake instead of a firm pump! [learn more](GNS213_U1_T3#GNS213_U1_T3_h3)

question: What common physical sensation do many patients report when experiencing a sudden heart dysrhythmia?
explanation: Patients frequently feel palpitations, which they describe as a racing, skipping, or fluttering sensation in their chest. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T3#GNS213_U1_T3_h4)

question: A patient has an apical pulse of 110 bpm, but a radial pulse of only 84 bpm. What does this gap mean?

options.A: The automatic blood pressure machine is malfunctioning
options.B: Many heartbeats are not strong enough to create a peripheral pulse wave
options.C: The patient is experiencing a severe drop in body temperature
options.D: The blood pressure cuff was wrapped too tightly around the arm

explanation: This is called a pulse deficit! The heart is beating away (110 times), but some beats are too weak to send a wave all the way down to the wrist. Always check both when you suspect rhythm trouble. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T3#GNS213_U1_T3_h4)

question: On a standard ECG tracing, what does the QRS complex show us?
explanation: Think of the QRS complex as the big electrical wave rushing through the lower chambers (ventricles), telling them it's time to squeeze and pump blood out to the body! [learn more](GNS213_U1_T3#GNS213_U1_T3_h5)

question: Why would a doctor order a 24-hour Holter monitor for a patient with occasional dizzy spells?

options.A: To continuously measure the oxygen saturation levels in the blood overnight
options.B: To deliver mild electrical shocks if the patient's heart rate drops too low
options.C: To catch intermittent dysrhythmias that do not happen during a quick clinic visit
options.D: To permanently replace the need for an invasive cardiac catheterization

explanation: Some heart flutters only happen once in a while. A 24-hour Holter monitor records the rhythm all day and night at home, helping catch those sneaky, unpredictable episodes! [learn more](GNS213_U1_T3#GNS213_U1_T3_h5)

question: What is the main goal of electrical cardioversion for a patient with a rapid, dangerous heart rhythm?

options.A: To permanently destroy the atrioventricular node
options.B: To reset the heart back to a normal sinus rhythm
options.C: To measure the exact cardiac output of the ventricles
options.D: To widen narrowed coronary arteries instantly

explanation: Cardioversion is like hitting 'restart' on a glitchy computer. It delivers a timed electrical shock to stop the chaos and let the heart's natural pacemaker take back control. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T3#GNS213_U1_T3_h6)

question: Which patient finding means you need to call for emergency help right away?

options.A: A heart rate of 102 beats per minute while walking
options.B: Blood pressure of 70/40 mmHg with altered mental status
options.C: Mild fatigue at the end of a normal daily work shift
options.D: Occasional fluttering sensations in the chest while resting

explanation: When blood pressure drops that low and the patient is confused, the bad rhythm is starving the brain and body of blood flow. That's an all-hands-on-deck emergency! [learn more](GNS213_U1_T3#GNS213_U1_T3_h6)

question: What is a dangerous mistake a nurse can make with bedside cardiac monitor alarms?

options.A: Checking the electrode patches daily for good skin contact
options.B: Setting individual alarm limits based on the patient's condition
options.C: Notifying the healthcare provider of persistent rhythm changes
options.D: Turning off or silencing the alarm limits completely

explanation: Never turn cardiac monitor alarms completely off! Alarm fatigue is real in busy wards, but silencing them entirely means a life-threatening rhythm change could be missed. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T3#GNS213_U1_T3_h7)

question: Why do patients with long-term atrial fibrillation often take blood thinners (anticoagulants)?

options.A: To strengthen the squeezing force of the left and right ventricular muscles
options.B: To slow down the electrical conduction speed through the atrioventricular node
options.C: To prevent blood clots from forming in the quivering atria and traveling to the brain
options.D: To lower systemic blood pressure and reduce strain on the coronary arteries

explanation: When the atria quiver instead of squeezing properly, blood sits still and can form clots. Blood thinners stop these clots from forming and traveling up to cause a stroke. Great clinical reasoning! [learn more](GNS213_U1_T3#GNS213_U1_T3_h7)
